content.value_statement: Educational short videos require research, clear animation, and careful music timing. This skill coordinates agent work and local tools to produce narration-free vertical videos.
actual_capabilities: Initialize a separate topic project with a rendering example, dependency manifests, reference timing data, and a production brief.
Guide the host agent through source checking, storyboarding, and topic-specific animation design.
Measure local audio onset strength, bass energy, event peaks, and candidate tempos.
Render a supplied Canvas animation example at 1440 by 2560 pixels and 30 frames per second.
Mix user-provided music and optional sound effects into H.264 video with AAC stereo audio.
Check video specifications, full decoding, and loudness, then generate a technical report and contact sheet.
limitations: Requires a capable host agent, Python 3.9+, Node.js 20+, FFmpeg, FFprobe, runtime libraries, and a CJK font.
Preparation copies an existing animation example; the host agent must research and implement scenes for each new topic.
Music and commercial fonts are not bundled; users must supply suitable files and confirm usage rights.
Visual acceptance requires image inspection or human review; complete Linux and Windows rendering has not been verified by the author.

use_cases.title: Explain a Scientific Concept
use_cases.description: Develop a short visual explanation with checked claims, readable captions, and animated comparisons.

use_cases.title: Produce a Consistent Video Series
use_cases.description: Reuse the reference layout and drawing methods while redesigning subjects, scenes, and music timing for each episode.

use_cases.title: Inspect an Animation Export
use_cases.description: Mix a compatible silent render with licensed music, inspect technical checks, and review sampled frames before delivery.

prompt_templates.title: Create a First Explainer
prompt_templates.prompt: Create a 60-second Chinese video explaining why the Moon has phases. Use my configured music and the default vertical format. Distinguish evidence from analogy.
prompt_templates.scenario: Beginner: produce a video from a clearly scoped topic.

prompt_templates.title: Plan Before Rendering
prompt_templates.prompt: Prepare only a researched storyboard about ocean tides. Include source references, caption text, scene timing, and visual explanations. Do not render a video yet.
prompt_templates.scenario: Intermediate: review narrative structure before committing rendering time.

prompt_templates.title: Adapt to Different Music
prompt_templates.prompt: Create a video explaining diffraction using the local music file [audio path]. Analyze its real events and redesign scene timing. Deliver the standard 2K30 MP4.
prompt_templates.scenario: Intermediate: synchronize new animation with a different audio track.

prompt_templates.title: Complete an Export Review
prompt_templates.prompt: Review my 60-second 1440 by 2560 silent render at [video path]. Mix [music path] from [start seconds] with [sound effects path]. Export without overwriting existing files. Report technical checks and any visual issues requiring human review.
prompt_templates.scenario: Advanced: finish an existing render with explicit inputs and acceptance checks.

output_examples.input: Prepare a new project explaining the phases of the Moon without configured music.
output: A separate project containing a production brief, animation example, dependency manifests, and reference timing materials.
Music status identifies missing configuration, so audio analysis remains incomplete.
Research and topic-specific scene design remain necessary before the example becomes a new explainer.

output_examples.input: Finish a compatible 60-second silent render using a supplied music track.
output: A vertical 1440 by 2560 MP4 at 30 frames per second with H.264 video and AAC stereo audio.
A technical report covering format checks, full decoding, measured loudness, and true peak.
A contact sheet and sampled frames for visual inspection; automated checks do not replace editorial review.

best_practices: Use a new project directory and retain source references for important claims.
Analyze the actual music segment and align animation events to its measured timing.
Inspect captions, transitions, and contact sheets, then review technical and loudness reports before delivery.
anti_patterns: Replace only the example captions while retaining unrelated objects, explanations, and timing.
Reuse reference beat analysis for a different track or segment without verification.
Claim visual or listening approval based only on automated checks, or use media without appropriate rights.

faq.question: What software does the workflow require?
faq.answer: It requires Python 3.9+, Node.js 20+, FFmpeg, FFprobe, NumPy, SciPy, Pillow, @napi-rs/canvas, and a CJK font.

faq.question: Does the skill generate voice narration?
faq.answer: No. The default format explains topics through animated visuals, short Chinese text, music, and optional sound effects.

faq.question: Is background music included?
faq.answer: No. Supply a local track through configuration, VIBE_MUSIC, or the music argument, and confirm that your intended use is permitted.

faq.question: Does project preparation generate a new topic automatically?
faq.answer: No. It copies a working example and creates a brief. The host agent must research the topic and rewrite its scenes.

faq.question: Do automated checks guarantee a finished video?
faq.answer: No. They check technical properties and audio measurements. A capable image tool or human must inspect readability, motion, and visual explanations.

faq.question: Can Claude, Codex, or Claude Code use this skill?
faq.answer: They need a host with skill loading, file access, terminal execution, research, and image inspection. Compatibility does not establish equivalent output quality.
